full.description: This is a microscopic histological image of lung tissue. The section shows alveoli containing numerous macrophages laden with fungal yeast forms typical of histoplasma pneumonia. The surrounding alveolar walls exhibit mild inflammatory changes and septal thickening. This appearance is characteristic of a pulmonary fungal infection such as histoplasmosis.

random.description: This is a photomicrograph of lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The alveolar spaces contain numerous round, pale, laminated foreign bodies, which are suggestive of exogenous material such as talc or starch granules. The surrounding lung parenchyma shows interstitial inflammation and multinucleated foreign body giant cells reacting to the material. These findings are characteristic of pulmonary talcosis or foreign body granulomatosis.
